bc_raven_s_cry_connector.blurb: Raven's Cry Connector is a small boulder field on the Sunshine Coast, in the forest of Sargeant Bay Provincial Park near Halfmoon Bay. There are five problems, running from V1 up to about V4+, and the stone is steep and often overhanging, with plenty of unclimbed lines still around. The block is shaded by trees, picks up some afternoon light, and is slow to dry after rain. Landings can be uneven and rough, with holes between the rocks, so bring several pads and scout carefully. Good for a short session combined with other bouldering nearby.

bc_echo_island_deep_water_soloing.blurb: Echo Island sits on Harrison Lake in the Fraser Valley, a short boat trip out from Harrison Hot Springs. This is deep water soloing: you climb with no rope or harness and fall into the lake, which runs roughly 30 to 85 feet deep. Cliffs and outcrops stretch along the shoreline, with steep to strongly overhanging walls and big roofs. There are five climbs, four of them boulder-style problems from about V3 to V6 and one 5.11 line. Warmer months are the best window, and the cold glacier-fed water and shifting wind deserve respect.

bc_bridge_river_valley.blurb: Bridge River Valley lies northeast of Lillooet and stretches along the road toward Carpenter Lake and Gold Bridge. It is a winter area built around long, multi-pitch ice and mixed lines, with big gullies, pillars and a canyon section. Of the five climbs here, four are water ice at WI4 and WI5, and one is a long trad line at moderate 5.7. Some routes are several hundred feet tall and a few are visible from the road. Many ice lines remain unclimbed. Several lines run through avalanche terrain, so heavy snow and late-season conditions call for caution.

bc_brandywine.blurb: Brandywine is a mountain climbing area in the Sea to Sky corridor, north of Squamish toward Whistler, reached up a forest service road. It is used for alpine outings in both summer and winter, and the climbing is bolted. There are five sport routes, from 5.7 into the 5.10 range, with a couple at 5.7, and one is a long multi-pitch outing. The setting is high and open, well above the lowland sport crags of the highway, and it doubles as a camping and hiking base for the nearby peaks. Expect a rough, steep road in.
